ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Comparison of Randomized Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Analytically compare the expected sample complexity of KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP, derive lower bounds for the convergence rate of each estimator, and compare these bounds to the existing results for LeverageSHAP.
CONTROLS: We will consider a class of regression problems with sparse feature vectors, and use the average case analysis for KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP, as has been done for LeverageSHAP's analysis.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: We expect to show that KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP exhibit similar convergence rates under the same conditions, and that unbiased KernelSHAP has slower convergence due to the added variance, but our experiments verifying these theorems could fail if the constants in the lower bounds are much larger than expected.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Sampling Distribution on KernelSHAP's Accuracy
PROPOSAL: Investigate how different sampling distributions (e.g., uniform, inverse kernel weight, and a distribution that attempts to maximize the variance of the kernel) affect the accuracy of KernelSHAP on various real-world datasets, and analyze the trade-offs between the sample efficiency, computational complexity, and accuracy of different sampling distributions.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with datasets such as IMDB, 20 Newsgroups, and HIGGS, which have varying complexity and size, and compare the accuracy of KernelSHAP under different sampling distributions using metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE).
COST: 28800
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the optimal sampling distribution for KernelSHAP depends on the characteristics of the dataset and that using a distribution that maximizes the variance of the kernel can lead to improved accuracy, but our experiments could fail if the kernel-based estimators fail to yield good approximations of the Shapley values even for large sample sizes.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Sampling Distribution on KernelSHAP's Accuracy and Computational Efficiency
PROPOSAL: Update the previous experiment to not only investigate the accuracy of KernelSHAP under different sampling distributions but also to analyze the trade-offs between the sample efficiency, computational complexity, and Shapley value computation time for each distribution. This will provide a comprehensive understanding of the benefits and drawbacks of each sampling distribution and help inform the choice of sampling distribution for practical applications.
CONTROLS: We will add new metrics such as Shapley value computation time, estimated by the number of matrix multiplications, and experiment with an additional sampling distribution that leverages the leverage score of the subsets to subsample the dataset.
COST: 38880
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the optimal sampling distribution for KernelSHAP depends on the characteristics of the dataset and that the benefits of using one sampling distribution over another will rely heavily on the computational resources available; our experiments could fail if the new sampling distributions fail to provide a meaningful advantage over the existing ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Empirical Study of Pairing and Sampling Without Replacement in KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Investigate the practical effects of pairing and sampling without replacement in KernelSHAP, two techniques implemented in the SHAP library to reduce sample complexity and improve accuracy. We will experiment with various datasets and analyze the impact of these techniques on the accuracy, sample efficiency, and computational complexity of KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with datasets such as IMDB, 20 Newsgroups, and HIGGS, and compare the results with and without pairing and sampling without replacement using metrics such as MAE and MSE.
COST: 55000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that pairing and sampling without replacement are effective techniques for improving the accuracy and reducing the sample complexity of KernelSHAP, but our experiments could fail if the benefits of these techniques are dependent on the specific characteristics of the dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Pretraining for Model-Agnostic Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Explore the idea of pretraining a model to estimate Shapley values, as proposed in SimSHAP. We will experiment with pretraining a model on a subset of the features and then using this model to estimate Shapley values for the entire feature set. Our goal is to investigate whether pretraining can improve the accuracy and sample efficiency of Shapley value estimation.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with pretraining a model on a subset of the features (e.g., 10% or 20% of the total features) and then using this model to estimate Shapley values for the entire feature set. We will compare the results with and without pretraining using metrics such as MAE and MSE.
COST: 77600
PREDICTION: We expect to find that pretraining can improve the accuracy and sample efficiency of Shapley value estimation, but our experiments could fail if pretraining introduces bias or overfitting to the subset of features used for pretraining.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Pretraining for Model-Agnostic Shapley Value Estimation with Optimized Hyperparameters
PROPOSAL: Update the previous experiment to include a grid search over the hyperparameters of the pretraining model and the Shapley value estimation model to optimize their performance. This will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the benefits and limitations of pretraining for Shapley value estimation.
CONTROLS: We will perform a grid search over the hyperparameters of the pretraining model (e.g., learning rate, batch size, number of hidden layers) and the Shapley value estimation model (e.g., kernel type, kernel width, regularization strength) to find the optimal combination of hyperparameters.
COST: 77600
PREDICTION: We expect to find that optimizing the hyperparameters of the pretraining and Shapley value estimation models can further improve the accuracy and sample efficiency of Shapley value estimation, but our experiments could fail if the optimal hyperparameters are highly dependent on the specific characteristics of the dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Leverage Score Sampling for Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of the expected sample complexity of Leverage Score Sampling for Shapley value estimation, and derive a bound on the error of the estimated Shapley values. This will provide a deeper understanding of the trade-offs between the sample complexity and accuracy of Leverage Score Sampling.
CONTROLS: We will assume a Gaussian distribution on the data and analyze the behavior of the leverage scores in this regime. We will also compare our theoretical results to empirical results on real-world datasets.
COST: 129600
PREDICTION: We expect to show that the leverage score sampling approach has a favorable trade-off between sample complexity and accuracy, but our analysis could fail if the leverage scores in practice deviate significantly from the assumed Gaussian distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Experimental Study of Shapley Value Estimation for High-Dimensional Data
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of various Shapley value estimation algorithms on high-dimensional datasets, including those with thousands of features. We will experiment with datasets such as the 20 Newsgroups dataset and the HIGGS dataset, and compare the results of Leverage Score Sampling, KernelSHAP, and other Shapley value estimation algorithms.
CONTROLS: We will use techniques such as PCA and feature selection to reduce the dimensionality of the data, and experiment with various hyperparameters to optimize the performance of each algorithm.
COST: 192000
PREDICTION: We expect to show that Leverage Score Sampling and other sampling-based algorithms outperform KernelSHAP and other Shapley value estimation algorithms on high-dimensional datasets, but our experiments could fail if the results are highly dependent on the specific characteristics of the dataset.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Beyond the Original Sampling Distribution: Investigating the Effect of Alternative Sampling Distributions on KernelSHAP's Performance
PROPOSAL: Update the previous experiment to investigate the effect of alternative sampling distributions on KernelSHAP's performance. We will experiment with various sampling distributions, such as stratified sampling and importance sampling, and compare their performance with the original sampling distribution.
CONTROLS: We will use the results from the previous experiment as a baseline and compare the performance of the alternative sampling distributions using metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE).
COST: 388800
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the alternative sampling distributions can improve the performance of KernelSHAP, but our experiments could fail if the improvements are too small to be significant or if the benefits of the alternative sampling distributions are dependent on the specific characteristics of the dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards a Unified Theory of Randomized Estimators for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Provide a unified theoretical framework for analyzing and comparing the performance of various randomized estimators for Shapley values, including KernelSHAP, Leverage Score Sampling, and others. This will enable the design of new estimators and the analysis of their properties in a principled manner.
CONTROLS: We will use tools from probability theory, statistics, and machine learning to develop a comprehensive theory of randomized estimators for Shapley values, and compare the performance of different estimators using various metrics.
COST: 460000
PREDICTION: We expect to develop a powerful and unified theory of randomized estimators for Shapley values, enabling the design of new and improved estimators and the analysis of their properties in a rigorous manner.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Multimodal Fusion Architectures for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of 4 different multimodal fusion architectures (early fusion, late fusion, attention-based fusion, and temporal convolutional network-based fusion) to generate natural-language descriptions of temporal change in satellite image time series. The comparison will be conducted on the Terra-MODIS dataset, evaluating 3 metrics: BLEU score, METEOR score, and CIDEr score for fluency and accuracy, and a temporal coherence metric specifically designed to assess how well the generated descriptions reflect the observed changes over time.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla transformer architecture without fusion, Baseline 2: simple interaction-based multimodal fusion.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that attention-based fusion and temporal convolutional network-based fusion outperform the other two architectures in terms of fluency and accuracy, while also achieving higher temporal coherence. However, it may struggle to capture complex, long-range dependencies in changes, which could lead to decreased performance when describing changes that occur over longer time periods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Transfer Learning for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of transfer learning on the performance of temporal change description and satellite image time series forecasting using the DeepOps  satellite image time series forecasting dataset. Specifically, we will fine-tune the pre-trained weights of a large-scale MLLM (e.g., LLaMA or PaLM) on a dataset of labeled satellite image time series, and then evaluate its performance on both tasks. We will also compare the performance of these fine-tuned models to that of their randomly initialized counterparts, as well as to models that are trained from scratch using only the satellite image time series data.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: MLLM trained from scratch using only the satellite image time series data, Baseline 2: MLLM with randomly initialized weights.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that transfer learning via fine-tuning improves performance on both tasks, particularly for the complex cases, and helps to adapt the MLLM to the specific domain. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning may depend on the quality and quantity of the pre-training data, and it may not generalize well to different domains or locations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a new metric to evaluate the temporal consistency of forecasts, and use it to compare the performance of different forecasting models on the DeepOps satellite image time series forecasting dataset. We will also investigate the relationship between this new metric and existing metrics, such as mean squared error (MSE) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR).
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: diffusion-based image generator without temporal consistency constraints, Baseline 2: temporal forecasting model with simple temporal consistency constraints (e.g., smoothness prior).
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that our new metric can effectively capture the temporal consistency of forecasts, and that models with strong temporal consistency constraints perform better on this metric. However, the relationship between the new metric and existing metrics may not be straightforward, and the effectiveness of the new metric may depend on the specific forecasting task and dataset.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a new metric, Temporal Inconsistency Score (TIS), to evaluate the temporal consistency of forecasts. TIS will be based on the discrepancy between the predicted changes and the observed trends in the historical data. We will then use TIS to compare the performance of different forecasting models, including a diffusion-based image generator with a novel temporal consistency loss function, and a temporal forecasting model with a dynamic temporal consistency constraint.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: diffusion-based image generator without temporal consistency constraints, Baseline 2: temporal forecasting model with simple temporal consistency constraints (e.g., smoothness prior).
COST: 5670
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that our new metric, TIS, can effectively capture the temporal consistency of forecasts, and that models with strong temporal consistency constraints perform better on this metric. However, the effect of TIS on the forecasting performance may not be direct, and the relationship between TIS and other metrics, such as MSE and PSNR, may be complex.

Note: I revised the third experiment to make it more specific and detailed, while keeping the core idea the same.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Temporal Sampling on Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate how different temporal sampling strategies (e.g., uniform, adaptive, sparse) affect the performance of satellite image time series forecasting models on the DeepOps dataset. We will also analyze the relationship between the sampling strategy and the temporal consistency of forecasts, as measured by TIS.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: uniform temporal sampling, Baseline 2: sparse temporal sampling, Baseline 3: adaptive temporal sampling.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that adaptive temporal sampling can improve the performance of forecasting models and increase temporal consistency, particularly in cases with sparse or irregularly sampled data. However, the effect of sampling strategy may depend on the specific dataset and forecasting task, and the choice of optimal sampling strategy may be problem-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Novel Temporal Fragmentation Approach for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel temporal fragmentation approach, which breaks down the long-term forecasting task into a set of shorter-term subtasks, and each subtask is solved using a different forecasting model. We will investigate the effectiveness of this approach on the DeepOps dataset, and compare it to traditional single-model-based approaches.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: single-model-based approach (e.g., diffusion-based image generator), Baseline 2: traditional hierarchical forecasting approach.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that the novel temporal fragmentation approach can improve the performance of forecasting models on long-term forecasting tasks, and provide a more flexible and adaptive framework for handling complex temporal dynamics. However, the effectiveness of this approach may depend on the specific dataset and forecasting task, and the choice of subtasks and models may be problem-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Role of Satellite Image Features in Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Investigate the importance of different satellite image features (e.g., spectral, spatial, temporal) in describing temporal changes in satellite image time series. We will use a range of machine learning techniques, including feature importance analysis and feature selection, to identify the most informative features and evaluate their impact on the performance of temporal change description models.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: model trained on all available features, Baseline 2: model trained on a subset of the most informative features.
COST: 13500
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that certain satellite image features are more informative than others for describing temporal changes, and that a focus on these features can improve the performance of temporal change description models. However, the effectiveness of feature selection may depend on the specific dataset and model architecture, and the choice of features may be problem-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of High-Resolution Satellite Imagery on Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of using high-resolution satellite imagery on the performance of temporal change description and forecasting models. We will compare the performance of models trained on high-resolution imagery to those trained on lower-resolution imagery, and evaluate the impact on both tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: model trained on lower-resolution imagery, Baseline 2: model trained on high-resolution imagery.
COST: 16200
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that models trained on high-resolution imagery perform better on both tasks, particularly on complex scenes with detailed spatial structures. However, the effect of high-resolution imagery may depend on the specific dataset and model architecture, and the increased computational requirements may be a limiting factor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Multi-Task Learning Framework for Satellite Image Time Series Analysis
PROPOSAL: Develop a multi-task learning framework that simultaneously trains models to perform both temporal change description and forecasting tasks. We will investigate the effectiveness of this approach on the DeepOps dataset, and compare it to single-task and joint-training approaches.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: single-task learning (description or forecasting), Baseline 2: joint-training approach (tasks shared with a single model).
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that a multi-task learning framework can improve the performance of models on both tasks, particularly when the tasks are closely related. However, the optimization of multiple loss functions and the selection of task weights may be challenging, and the effectiveness of this approach may depend on the specific dataset and model architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation of the Dataset Shift and Model Generalizability on Satellite Image Time Series Analysis Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of dataset shift and model generalizability on the performance of models trained on the DeepOps dataset. We will evaluate the performance of models on an independent test set from a different region or with different environmental and climate conditions, and analyze the impact of dataset shift on the performance of models with and without transfer learning.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: model trained and evaluated on the same dataset, Baseline 2: model trained on a different dataset and evaluated on the DeepOps dataset.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: This experiment is expected to show that models with transfer learning can generalize better to new datasets and regions, and perform better on the tasks of temporal change description and forecasting. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning may depend on the specific dataset and model architecture, and the optimal hyperparameters for transfer learning may need to be tuned for each task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Parameter Selection for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel method called "active parameter selection" that learns to dynamically select the most relevant model parameters to update online, based on a combination of past performance and current distribution shift.
CONTROLS: Compare with methods updating final-layer weights, adapter modules, and all model parameters; use metrics of mean absolute error (MAE) and dynamic regret.
COST: 56700
PREDICTION: Active parameter selection is expected to outperform the baselines, especially in scenarios with significant distribution shift, but might struggle with high-dimensional models and large parameter spaces where the method's adaptability is less effective; the results might not generalize well to other domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Update Strategies for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We investigate various adaptive update strategies for multi-step forecasting, including gradient filtering, recency-weighted aggregation, and exponentially weighted averages, to mitigate the effects of delayed and noisy feedback.
CONTROLS: Compare with vanilla online gradient descent (OGD), experience replay (ER), and multistep gradient descent (MSGD); test on a variety of forecasting tasks, including traffic flow, electricity consumption, and solar power forecasting, using metrics of MAE and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).
COST: 105600
PREDICTION: Adaptive update strategies are expected to significantly improve performance over OGD and ER, while MSGD is expected to be more computationally expensive but also more effective; the best strategy might depend on the specific forecasting task and dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distributed Memory for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a distributed memory-based method that selects a subset of past data samples to store in memory, enabling efficient aggregation of historical information without the need for experience replay.
CONTROLS: Compare with methods using ER, as well as a baseline with no memory; evaluate on traffic flow and electricity consumption forecasting datasets using MAE and MAPE metrics.
COST: 158400
PREDICTION: The distributed memory method is expected to outperform ER and the baseline, especially on tasks with high variability and concept drift, as it allows for efficient updating of the model based on the most relevant historical data; however, the method may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to select the optimal subset of samples.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Distributed Memory with Neighborhood Learning
PROPOSAL: We extend the distributed memory-based method from proposal 3 to include a neighborhood learning component, which examines the model's predictions for nearby instances in memory and refines the model's parameters accordingly.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original distributed memory method and a local-only model, as well as a no-memory baseline.
COST: 158400
PREDICTION: The revised distributed memory method is expected to improve performance over the original method, especially on tasks where local patterns are informative; however, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to balance local and global adaptation.

Note: We're revising proposal 3 to incorporate a more sophisticated neighborhood learning component, which can help improve performance and adaptability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Online Forecasting Model Selection
PROPOSAL: We introduce a meta-learning approach that selects the most suitable forecasting model for a given scenario from a pre-trained set of models, allowing for adaptation to changing conditions and distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: Compare with a fixed-model approach, as well as a no-meta-learning baseline with a validator choosing among set models randomly; evaluate on a diverse set of datasets, including traffic flow, electricity consumption, and solar power forecasting.
COST: 259200
PREDICTION: The meta-learning approach is expected to outperform the fixed-model approach and the no-meta-learning baseline, especially in scenarios with significant distribution shift; however, it may be computationally expensive and require careful tuning of meta-learning objectives and hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Transfer Learning for Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose an online transfer learning approach that adapts a pre-trained forecasting model to a new, unseen environment with minimal additional data, leveraging the knowledge and patterns learned from previous environments.
CONTROLS: Compare with a fine-tuning approach, as well as a no-transfer-learning baseline with a new, randomly initialized model; test on a set of traffic flow and electricity consumption forecasting datasets with varying levels of seasonal and trend components.
COST: 377600
PREDICTION: The online transfer learning approach is expected to significantly improve adaptation and generalization performance over the fine-tuning approach and the no-transfer-learning baseline, especially in scenarios with limited new data; however, it may be prone to overfitting to previous environments and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bayesian Online Learning for Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a Bayesian online learning approach that integrates a probabilistic forecasting model with a online variational inference algorithm, enabling rigorous uncertainty quantification and adaptive updates in the presence of distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: Compare with a deterministic online learning approach, as well as a no-learning baseline with a fixed model; evaluate on a set of weather forecasting and exchange rate forecasting datasets with varying levels of noise and non-linearity.
COST: 602900
PREDICTION: The Bayesian online learning approach is expected to provide more reliable and accurate forecasts, as well as uncertainty estimates, compared to the deterministic online learning approach and the no-learning baseline; however, it may be computationally more expensive due to the need for online variational inference and may require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Adaptive Gradient Clipping for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We extend the efficient parameter selection method from proposal 1 to include adaptive gradient clipping, which dynamically adjusts the learning rate based on the estimated gradient norm, ensuring stable and efficient updates.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original parameter selection method and a gradient descent-based method without parameter selection.
COST: 56700
PREDICTION: The revised method is expected to improve stability and convergence speed compared to the original method and the gradient descent-based method, while preserving the benefits of efficient parameter selection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture of Experts for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a mixture of experts approach that combines the predictions of multiple specialized forecasting models, each optimized for a different time horizon or type of data, to achieve robust and adaptive online forecasting.
CONTROLS: Compare with a single-model approach and an ensemble learning approach without expertise; test on a diverse set of datasets, including traffic flow, electricity consumption, and solar power forecasting.
COST: 1136000
PREDICTION: The mixture of experts approach is expected to outperform the single-model approach and the ensemble learning approach, especially in scenarios with complex dynamics and distribution shifts; however, it may be computationally expensive and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Recency-Weighted Adaptive Update Strategies for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We refine the adaptive update strategies for multi-step forecasting from proposal 2 by incorporating recency-weighted averaging, which gives more importance to recent updates and helps reduce the impact of delayed and noisy feedback.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original adaptive update strategies and a naive update strategy without recency weighting; evaluate on a set of traffic flow and electricity consumption forecasting datasets with varying numbers of steps ahead.
COST: 105600
PREDICTION: The revised adaptive update strategies are expected to outperform the original and naive update strategies, especially in scenarios with high variability and delayed feedback; however, they may be computationally more expensive and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

Note: We're revising proposal 2 to incorporate recency-weighted averaging, which can help improve the adaptive update strategies for multi-step forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of a Lightweight Dense Text retriever on Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of a multimodal retriever that combines a vision-centric ColPali-base encoder with a lightweight dense text retriever, such as the Annoy implementation of FAISS, on visual document retrieval benchmarks likeƯ Wisconsin-MUltiple Choice (WiMUC) and ANDI Image Ranking.
CONTROLS: Baseline: ColPali-base encoder alone, ablation: removing the dense text retriever
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect to see an improvement in Mean Average Precision (MAP) when combining the two retrievers, especially on datasets with diverse visual and textual features. However, if the dense text retriever is too weak, the performance may degrade, highlighting the challenges of combining heterogeneous models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency-Aware Hybrid Retriever for Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel hybrid retrieval approach that leverages a latency-aware fusion strategy to combine the outputs of the vision-centric ColPali-base encoder and the dense text retriever from proposal 1. This strategy involves dynamically adjusting the weight of each retriever based on the available latency and memory budgets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Randomly sampling the dynamically adjusted weight, ablation: fixed latency budget or eliminating the dense text retriever
COST: 8100
PREDICTION: By adaptively adjusting the weights, we expect to see a significant improvement in the trade-off between retrieval quality (MAP) and online latency, especially on datasets with high diversity and sparsity in visual features. However, if the latency-aware strategy is too complex, it might introduce additional latency, making the overall system less efficient.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Multi-Vector Aggregation Techniques for Combining Heterogeneous Representations
PROPOSAL: Investigate and compare various multi-vector aggregation techniques, such as concatenation, Hadamard product, and late fusion with MRR, to combine the dense text retriever's output with the vision-centric ColPali-base encoder's output. This will help identify the most effective aggregation strategy for exploiting the rich query-document interactions within each model's representation space.
CONTROLS: Baseline: simple concatenation, ablation: different aggregation techniques (e.g., element-wise multiplication, stack-based aggregation)
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: We expect to see varying degrees of improvement in MAP when using different aggregation techniques, with some techniques yielding significant gains while others leading to decreased performance. However, identifying the most effective technique might be challenging due to the high dimensionality and variability of the combined feature space.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Document Diversification on Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Reconsider proposal 1's experiments and shift the focus from combining a lightweight dense text retriever with a ColPali-base encoder to exploring how document diversification techniques, such as sampling from a dataset, can help mitigate the high latency and storage overhead associated with large document representations. This involves analyzing the effects of diversification on retrieval quality, online latency, and index memory usage.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform sampling, ablation: alternative sampling strategies (e.g., importance sampling, reservoir sampling)
COST: 12600
PREDICTION: By adaptively sampling documents, we expect to see improved trade-offs between retrieval quality (MAP), online latency, and index memory usage. However, effectively applying document diversification techniques in real-world scenarios may be more challenging than anticipated, requiring careful tuning and balancing between these competing factors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval in Low-Rank Regimes
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of hybrid retrieval in scenarios where both the primary and secondary retrievers operate in low-rank regimes (i.e., using factorized or reduced-dimensional representations). This involves deriving bounds on the expected performance of the combined retriever and exploring the relationship between the ranks of the two encoders and the achievable quality of the final retrieval results.
CONTROLS: None required, as the goal is to provide a theoretical foundation for the practical results obtained by proposals 1-3.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: The derived bounds will provide valuable insights into the conditions under which hybrid retrieval can be expected to improve the performance of vision-centric multimodal encoders. However, the applicability of the theoretical analysis might be limited to scenarios in which the low-rank regimes exhibit sparse or simplifiable behavior, which may not be representative of the real-world datasets used in proposals 1-3.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation of Hyperparameter Tuning Strategies for Hybrid Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Investigate and compare the effectiveness of different hyperparameter tuning strategies for the hybrid retriever proposed in proposal 2. This involves analyzing the impact of various objective functions (e.g., MAP, precision at k, normalized discounted cumulative gain), search algorithms (e.g., random search, grid search, Bayesian optimization), and evaluation metrics on the performance of the hybrid retriever on visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: random search with MAP as the objective function, ablation: using alternative objective functions, search algorithms, or evaluation metrics
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect to see varying degrees of improvement in the performance of the hybrid retriever when employing different hyperparameter tuning strategies. However, the choice of the best strategy might be highly dependent on the specific characteristics of the benchmark datasets and the trade-offs prioritized in the application.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Robustness of Hybrid Retrievers to Adversarial Perturbations
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the robustness of the hybrid retriever proposed in proposal 2 to adversarial perturbations in the input query or document representations. This involves generating perturbed inputs using various attack methods (e.g., FGSM, PGD, adversarial training) and analyzing the impact of these perturbations on the performance of the hybrid retriever on visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: unperturbed inputs, ablation: different attack methods, perturbation budgets, or attack targets (e.g., query, document, both)
COST: 34000
PREDICTION: We expect to see a decrease in the performance of the hybrid retriever when faced with adversarial perturbations, which could be mitigated by incorporating robustness-promoting techniques (e.g., adversarial training, input denoising) into the hybrid retriever architecture. However, the design of effective defenses against adversarial attacks is a challenging problem, and the best approach may depend on the specific application and dataset used.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation of Gradient-Based Hyperparameter Tuning Methods for Hybrid Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Reconsider proposal 5's experiments and shift the focus from random search and grid search to gradient-based methods for hyperparameter tuning, such as gradient descent with a path length penalty or natural gradient descent, to find the optimal hyperparameters for the hybrid retriever.
CONTROLS: Baseline: gradient descent with constant step size, ablation: different optimization algorithms, penalty functions, or regularization techniques
COST: 29110
PREDICTION: By leveraging gradient information, we expect to see faster convergence and more efficient hyperparameter tuning for the hybrid retriever. However, the choice of the best gradient-based method might depend on the specific characteristics of the benchmark datasets and the trade-offs prioritized in the application.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Case Study: Integrating Hybrid Retrieval with a Production-Ready Visual Document Retrieval System
PROPOSAL: Collaborate with the developers of a production-ready visual document retrieval system to integrate the hybrid retriever from proposal 2 into their existing infrastructure. This involves evaluating the performance and efficiency of the hybrid retriever in a real-world scenario and investigating the practical benefits and challenges of deploying hybrid retrieval in a production environment.
CONTROLS: Baseline: existing retrieval system, ablation: comparing performance metrics with and without the hybrid retriever
COST: 61200
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant benefits from integrating the hybrid retriever, including improved retrieval quality and reduced latency, in the production-ready system. However, we may also encounter unforeseen challenges or limitations during the integration process, requiring iterative refinement and adaptation to meet the system's requirements.
